title: Fake AI job candidates pass interviews and vanish, Arena CEO says
excerpt: Arena's cofounder and CEO says fake job candidates passed interviews with the company's engineers and then disappeared.
content_html:
Arena's CEO says his company has encountered job applicants who seem too good to be true — literally.

Anastasios Angelopoulos said that the AI-model evaluation company he cofounded has interviewed candidates who turned out to be AI rather than real people.

"They're passing all of our technical interviews," Angelopoulos said in an interview on the "20VC" podcast that aired on Monday.

"And then what happens at the end of it? You try to hire them, and it's vaporware," he added, referring to an industry term for a product that never materializes.

He described the applicants as "fake people applying to companies," adding that Arena's engineers had interviewed the candidates and believed they were real.

"This person wasn't real. It was AI," he said.

Angelopoulos did not say how Arena had determined the applicants were AI-generated.

He said he did not know who was behind the bogus applications, but raised the possibility of corporate espionage, cyberattacks, or attempts to access company data and code.

Arena didn't immediately reply to a request for comment from Business Insider.

The rise of fake candidates

Angelopoulos said fake candidates were pushing Arena to consider requiring new hires to complete onboarding in person.

"If you want a laptop, you got to come to the office. We got to go and shake your hand. We got to verify that you're real," Angelopoulos said.

"People are trying to get into all of the American businesses," Angelopoulos added. "We're not the only ones. This is happening everywhere."

It's not the first time US companies have confronted fake job candidates involving AI, although the scale can vary from individual scammers to coordinated nation-state schemes.

In a 2025 alert, the FBI warned that North Korean IT workers had used AI and face-swapping technology in video interviews to conceal their identities and secure remote roles at US companies.

The bureau said some workers then used unlawful access to steal proprietary and sensitive data after obtaining employment with more than 100 US companies.

It urged employers to verify identities during interviews and onboarding — ideally in person — and to continue checks throughout remote workers' employment.

Several tech companies have since moved to block bogus job applications. Coinbase required all workers to come to the US for in-person orientation, while Amazon has used AI to screen and block applications from suspected North Korean agents.

While the exact number of companies facing fake AI job candidates is unclear, Gartner, a technology research and advisory firm, found in a second-quarter 2025 survey of 3,000 job candidates that 6% admitted taking part in interview fraud — either posing as someone else or having someone else pose as them in an interview.

Gartner said it expects one in four candidate profiles worldwide to be fake by 2028.

安杰洛普洛斯在周一播出的“20VC”播客上接受采访时表示：“他们正在通过我们所有的技术面试。”

“然后最后会发生什么呢？ 你试图雇用他们，但它是蒸气软件，”他补充道，他指的是从未实现的产品的行业术语。

他将这些申请人描述为“申请公司的假人”，并补充说 Arena 的工程师已经面试了这些候选人，并相信他们是真实的。

“这个人不是真实的。 这是人工智能，”他说。

安杰洛普洛斯没有透露 Arena 如何确定申请人是人工智能生成的。

他表示，他不知道这些虚假应用程序的幕后黑手是谁，但提出了企业间谍活动、网络攻击或试图访问公司数据和代码的可能性。

Arena 没有立即回复《商业内幕》的置评请求。

假候选人的兴起

安杰洛普洛斯表示，假候选人正在推动 Arena 考虑要求新员工亲自完成入职。

“如果你想要一台笔记本电脑，你就必须来办公室。 我们得去和你握手。 我们必须验证你的真实性，”安杰洛普洛斯说道。

安杰洛普洛斯补充道：“人们正试图进入所有美国企业。” “我们不是唯一的人。 这种事到处都在发生。”

这并不是美国公司第一次遇到涉及人工智能的虚假求职者，尽管规模可能从个人诈骗者到协调一致的民族国家计划有所不同。

美国联邦调查局 (FBI) 在 2025 年警报中警告称，朝鲜 IT 员工在视频采访中使用人工智能和换脸技术来隐藏自己的身份，并确保在美国公司担任远程角色。

该局表示，一些员工在 100 多家美国公司就业后，利用非法访问手段窃取专有和敏感数据。

它敦促雇主在面试和入职期间验证身份（最好是亲自验证），并在远程工人的整个就业过程中继续进行检查。

此后，多家科技公司已采取行动阻止虚假的工作申请。 Coinbase 要求所有员工前往美国进行现场培训，而亚马逊则使用人工智能来筛选和阻止可疑的朝鲜特工的申请。

虽然面临虚假人工智能求职者的公司的确切数量尚不清楚，但技术研究和咨询公司 Gartner 在 2025 年第二季度对 3000 名求职者进行的调查中发现，6% 的人承认参与了面试欺诈——要么冒充别人，要么让别人冒充自己参加面试。

Gartner 表示，预计到 2028 年，全球四分之一的候选人资料将是虚假的。
